findings.title: Data race on shared `err` variable in index-build errgroup
findings.body: In `searchSupport.init`, each `group.Go` closure assigns to the function-scoped `err` variable (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and `totalBatchesIndexed++` is incremented without synchronization. With `initWorkers > 1` these run concurrently, producing a genuine data race: build errors can be lost or overwritten (and `group.Wait()`'s result can be confused with a stale value), and the counter can be wrong. This matters more now that the coarse lock in `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` was removed, so the goroutines actually run in parallel. Use a local `err :=` inside the closure and an atomic counter.

findings.title: Concurrent BuildIndex for the same key can collide on the bleve directory and cache entry
findings.body: BuildIndex no longer holds `cacheMu` for the whole function; the lock is only taken when writing the cache. Two concurrent calls for the same NamespacedResource (e.g. a watch event triggering `getOrCreateIndex` while startup indexing runs) will both call `bleve.New(dir, ...)` on the same path, which fails (or corrupts) for file-backed indexes, and both will write to `b.cache[key]`, so one fully built index is silently discarded while readers may already hold it. Consider per-key locking / single-flight instead of no lock at all.

findings.title: TotalDocs reads the cache map without holding cacheMu
findings.body: `TotalDocs` iterates `b.cache` without taking `cacheMu` (even read lock). Previously writes to the map happened while BuildIndex held the exclusive lock for its entire duration; now writes are short but can occur from watch-event-driven builds at any time. `init()` in search.go now calls `s.search.TotalDocs()` while such builds can be in flight, so a concurrent map read/write panic is possible. Take `cacheMu.RLock()` in TotalDocs.

findings.title: Context/goroutine leak when Init fails in NewResourceServer
findings.body: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` on failure, but the `cancel` from `context.WithCancel` created a few lines above is never called on this path. The derived context stays alive, and any goroutines already started by `s.search.init` (the watch-event consumer goroutine started before the failure point) are never stopped. Add `defer`/explicit `cancel()` before returning the error.

findings.title: Stop() no longer prevents further request handling
findings.body: `Stop()` sets `s.initErr = "service is stopping"/"service is stopped"` as the mechanism to reject requests, but all the `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil` guards were removed from Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/Blob handlers. After `Stop()` those handlers will keep serving requests against a cancelled background context and a stopped backend, instead of returning an error. Either re-add a lightweight 'is running' check to the handlers or drop the now-dead initErr mutation in Stop.
